Last week, Bloomberg reported that Apple is developing a screenless fitness tracker, similar to WHOOP or Fitbit Air. Having been a WHOOP user for six months, I agree the concept is solid, but there are a few things I hope Apple can do better.

At present, details about Apple's screenless fitness tracker are scarce, as the product is still in very early development. The earliest it could launch is 2028. Bloomberg described it as "a slim fabric band with a built-in sensor-equipped computing module."

Earlier this year, WHOOP ran a promotion with Chase where you could get a WHOOP at a discount or even free if you had a Chase Sapphire card, and I took advantage of that. I've been using WHOOP since then, but I wouldn't say I've fully committed to it.

The reason is simple: automatic workout detection is never perfect, and I find it annoying to have to pull out my phone to log a workout — whether starting it before or adding it after. With Apple Watch, you can start a workout right from the watch face. WHOOP syncs the time back from Apple Health — that's actually the main reason I still wear my Apple Watch.

Pulling out my phone at the gym is tolerable, but for something casual like a bike ride or a walk, I'd rather not bother with my phone.

So for Apple's screenless fitness tracker, I'd really like to see physical buttons and indicator lights that can start and stop workout recording. You may still need your phone afterwards to categorise the workout, but I'd rather deal with that after than during the activity. Apple could also consider building classification models based on certain data points.

The Bottom Line

If Apple can pull off a screenless fitness tracker that doesn't constantly rely on your phone, I think it would be very appealing. The form factor has many advantages, including comfort, longer battery life, and the ability to wear it alongside a traditional watch.

The most popular comment, posted by TB

I bought a FitBit Air because I'd been wearing an Apple Watch for nearly a year and was starting to feel fatigued by it. I like going back to mechanical watches, but I also want to keep tracking my health data and still enjoy the conveniences of a smartwatch, like not having to pull out my phone (e.g. for quick Apple Pay, unlocking doors when my hands are full, etc.). If Apple makes something fully integrated into the ecosystem — where I can use a pared-down Apple Pay, door key, car key, and other NFC features, plus connect to AirPods so Siri can read messages and act on my behalf — I'd be first in line to buy it.

Honestly, after evaluating WHOOP for myself, I prefer a smartwatch, even if it means accepting shorter battery life. I get that some people like the screenless design for its focus and lack of distractions, but personally, I just turn on Do Not Disturb mode on my watch and call it a day.

What do you think about Apple developing a screenless fitness tracker? What price would it take for you to buy one? Share your thoughts in the comments.
